Conclusion: All twenty complete cycles and forty encoding cleanups passed the unchanged bounded gate: +3 median handles and +2,322,432 private bytes. Exactly one player was created and disposed, with forty distinct playback IDs and source-clear checks; all forty native HTTP filters were disposed. Final idle handles were 1292, 1292, and 1272. This isolates repeated player creation/retirement as a relevant resource boundary in the tested sequential path. It does not prove the managed product HTTP path, concurrent cancellation, fallback, stale-callback isolation, or product acceptance.
